subject: Urgent: Hosted API 429 feedback storm impacting Sentra Health — p95/p99 regressions
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sentrahealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spike / 429s hitting our production workflows

Irene / Monica —

We started seeing a large increase in p95/p99 latency around 07:45 PDT this morning for calls routed to your hosted endpoint (model: rwd-13b-v2). Concurrently our retry logic observed a surge of 429s and we saw a cascading set of timeouts on our side (multiple downstream jobs retried). Attaching a short timeline and a few request IDs.

Impact: several clinical batch jobs timed out, one near-miss on a patient alert pipeline (we had to fail open). This is high-severity for us — can you confirm whether rate limiting or gateway retries are being applied that would amplify a feedback loop?

Request IDs (sample): req_9Y1, req_9Y2, req_9Y9
Attachments: p95-p99-graphs-20270615.png, request-ids-sample-logs.txt

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Platform Engineer
Sentra Health
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sentrahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spike / 429s hitting our production workflows

Alex —

Thanks for the quick note and the artifacts. I’m escalating this to our SRE/ops team — Monica and Rafael are on it now. Initial hypothesis from our side: a short-lived upstream concurrency burst combined with aggressive client retries can cause token-queueing that amplifies tail latency, and our rate limiter can then return 429s which clients (if configured for simple exponential backoff without jitter) may retry immediately, creating a feedback storm.

We’ll investigate the following in parallel:
- verify whether any routing changes or model variants were promoted around 07:30–08:00 PDT
- look for request fanout patterns from your keys (many parallel requests with same prefix)
- sample backend queues and KV-cache hit rates for the affected nodes
- check our rate-limiter logs to confirm whether we returned 429s and why

I’ll circle back with a timeline within 90 minutes.

— Irene
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sentrahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spike / 429s hitting our production workflows

I dug into the gateway logs for Sentra’s API key between 07:30–09:00 PDT. Findings so far:
- We observed a ~4x increase in concurrent inflight requests for that key at 07:46.
- Our rate limiter began returning 429s when token bucket fell below threshold at 07:48 on several hosts.
- There are approximately 2000 client-side retries within a 2-minute window that line up with the 429 surge — retry timings look too tight (initial backoff 200ms, no jitter).
- A small subset of requests show request fanout (single upstream trigger fanouts to 8 downstream calls).

Preliminary mitigation steps I’ve started:
1) Temporarily increased per-key burst allowance on a small set of nodes handling Sentra traffic to reduce immediate 429s (will revert after stabilization)
2) Enabled additional request tracing and captured KV-cache hit rates for the affected nodes
3) Coordinated with runtime to throttle aggressive retry loops via a per-key soft limit that normalizes behavior over 30s

I’m going to escalate to Markus for cross-cluster coordination if we see persistent queueing. Rafael, can you pull the host-level queue lengths and GPU utilization for the affected pool and share ASAP?

— Monica
Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sentrahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spike / 429s hitting our production workflows

Update from infra:
- Host queue depth spiked to ~5x normal on pool-gamma between 07:45–08:05 PDT; GPU utilization climbed to 92% on several nodes, with increased kernel queuing for attention ops.
- KV-cache hit rate dropped ~18% for Sentra's prefix; we saw more cold-start decoding ops which increased tail latency per request.
- Our rate limiter logs show ~17K 429 responses across the cluster targeting Sentra’s key window 07:48–08:02.

Immediate actions applied:
- Drained a subset of queued work onto an adjacent pool (warm nodes) to reduce queuing pressure.
- Applied a temporary model-variant fallback for long-context requests to a slightly more quantized variant (rwd-13b-v2-q4) for the next 20 minutes to reduce per-token compute.
- Deployed a short-lived adaptive backoff rule that inserts randomized jitter into server-suggested Retry-After for that key — this should reduce synchronized client retries.

I recommend Sentra consider widening client retry backoff and adding jitter; we can provide recommended settings. Markus will coordinate a follow-up runbook for preventing recurrence.

— Rafael
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sentrahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spike / 429s hitting our production workflows

Looping in exec ops per account impact and asking for prioritization:
- Sentra experienced real customer-visible incidents (timers exceeded, alert pipeline degraded). We should treat this as P1 for dedicated follow-up: postmortem, recommended client-side retry config, and a controls checklist for increasing per-key burst safely.

Proposed short deliverables (ETA in hours):
1) Ops timeline & root-cause summary (Rafael / Monica) — 4 hours
2) Recommended client retry policy and sample code (Monica) — 6 hours
3) Postmortem and runbook including guardrails for rapid per-key burst changes (Markus / Rafael) — 24 hours

Irene — can you coordinate Sentra exec update and ask for a short maintenance window to test the soft-fallback variant?

— Marissa
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sentrahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spike / 429s hitting our production workflows

Alex —

Thank you again for flagging this so quickly. Summary for Sentra execs (short):
- What happened: short, high-concurrency burst caused KV-cache pressure and GPU queueing; our rate limiter returned many 429s while clients retried aggressively, producing a feedback storm that amplified tail latency (p95/p99 regressions).
- Immediate mitigations we applied: raised safe per-key burst on a subset of hosts, drained queues to adjacent pools, deployed a temporary quantized model variant for long-context requests, and added server-side jittered retry guidance.
- Next steps (we will deliver per Marissa’s plan): Ops timeline, recommended client retry config (including randomized exponential backoff sample), and a runbook for per-key burst adjustments + guardrails.

Could we schedule a 30-minute post-incident call with Sentra SRE at 17:00 PDT today to run through the timeline and agree on client-side retry limits? Please confirm availability.

I’ll also share the sample retry policy and a short checklist for your engineering leads before the call.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
